newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas corn planting nears completion.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas corn planting nears completion.

text.p: The Arkansas corn crop was 99 percent seeded as of Sunday, topping the five-year average of 95 percent, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
The crop was rated two percent poor, 50 percent fair, 38 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Soybeans were 25 percent planted, against 26 percent last year and 17 percent for the five-year average. Twelve percent of the crop had emerged, compared with nine percent average.
Wheat was 100 percent headed, above last year's 96 percent and the five-year average of 96 percent.
The crop was rated two percent very poor, 20 percent poor, 49 percent fair, 25 percent good and four percent excellent.
Cotton was 86 percent seeded versus 70 percent on average.
Rice was 90 percent planted, above the five-year average of 80 percent. The crop was 57 percent emerged.
Soil moisture was rated 31 percent short, 67 percent adequate and 2 percent surplus.
Livestock was said to be in good condition statewide, but no pasture or range conditions were given.
